body:
So it is C++ specific, we can only repro on the ci machine. /cc @gunan fyi

It fails when building `//tensorflow/core:lib_internal`:
```
$ bazel build -c opt --distinct_host_configuration=false -- tensorflow/core:lib_internal   
INFO: Reading 'startup' options from /etc/bazel.bazelrc: --batch
INFO: Found 1 target...
Target //tensorflow/core:lib_internal failed to build
ERROR: /Users/jenkins/workspace/tensorflow-cl-mac/tensorflow/core/BUILD:1152:1 Failed to get cached inputs: Could not determine containing package for external/snappy/snappy.h.
INFO: Elapsed time: 4.563s, Critical Path: 0.06s
```

Content of the .bazelrc:
```
build -s
build --define with_gcp_support=true
build --define with_hdfs_support=true
```

Content of /etc/bazel.bazelrc:
```
# Running bazel inside a `docker build` command causes trouble, cf:
#   https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/134
# The easiest solution is to set up a bazelrc file forcing --batch.
startup --batch

# Similarly, we need to workaround sandboxing issues:
#   https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/418
build  --verbose_failures --spawn_strategy=standalone --genrule_strategy=standalone
test --spawn_strategy=standalone

# Force bazel output to use colors (good for jenkins) and print useful errors.
common --color=yes

# Configure tests - increase timeout, print errors and timeout warnings
test --verbose_failures --test_output=errors --test_verbose_timeout_warnings
```

Tracing the code, I think it can only happen in these circumstances:
- sandboxing disabled
- remote repository removed from WORKSPACE file
- the command line must be identical otherwise we don't try to use the cache
- header file previously found through -isystem
- but the same -isystem still must be in the command-line

- --strict_system_includes not set

There's a trivial fix for what I believe to be the underlying issue, but I want to have a reproduction before I make that change.
